s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic respiratory symptoms with systemic lymphadenopathy and multi-organ involvement
salient_findings: Difficulties in breathing, cough, and expectoration for more than 30 days
Fever for more than 15 days
Multiple enlarged lymph nodes in the neck and abdomen regions
Cavities in the right upper anterior mediastinum and nodular shadow in the lower part of both lungs
Bilateral adrenal masses and multiple lesions in both lungs
key_facts: Presenting symptoms: difficulties in breathing, cough, and expectoration
Duration of symptoms: more than 30 days
Past medical history: hyperuricemia for 5 years
Enlarged lymph nodes in the neck and abdomen regions
Cavities in the right upper anterior mediastinum
Nodular shadow in the lower part of both lungs
Bone destruction of right clavicle and thoracic 11 right pedicle
Lymphadenopathy in neck and abdomen regions
Lesions in right lobe of thyroid gland

shortlist.label: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple enlarged lymph nodes, lymphadenopathy, and lesions in various organs

shortlist.label: Hodgkin lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Systemic lymphadenopathy, cavities in mediastinum, and nodular shadows in lungs

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Multi-organ involvement, lymphadenopathy, and granulomatous lesions

shortlist.label: Lymphomatoid granulomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Nodular shadows in lungs, lymphadenopathy, and lesions in multiple organs

shortlist.label: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive lymphoma with systemic involvement, lymphadenopathy, and multi-organ lesions

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of enlarged lymph nodes, multiple lesions in both lungs, bilateral adrenal masses, and bone destruction, along with the biopsy findings of proliferative lymphoid tissues and singular large heterotypic proliferative lymphoid cells, are highly suggestive of Non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

rejected.label: Hodgkin lymphoma
rejected.why: While Hodgkin lymphoma could explain some symptoms, the biopsy findings and the presence of singular large heterotypic proliferative lymphoid cells are more characteristic of Non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Sarcoidosis typically presents with granulomatous inflammation, which is not indicated in the biopsy findings.

rejected.label: Lymphomatoid granulomatosis
rejected.why: This condition is a rare form of lymphoma, but the biopsy findings do not specifically suggest this diagnosis over Non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

rejected.label: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: While this is a subtype of Non-Hodgkin lymphoma, the information provided does not specifically differentiate it from other forms of Non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
